title: Microsoft Agent 365: the control plane for agents in the admin centre
summary: Hold: Microsoft publishes user-level licensing requirements that the briefing reports as unpublished, and documents a package API covering MCP servers despite the claimed automation gap. Ownership reassignment also needs its documented agent-type restriction. The listed navigation paths and inventory and block calls are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for blocking an MCP server.
claims.quote: A package represents an agent or a tool, such as a plugin, MCP server, or skill, in the organization catalog. ... Block, unblock, and reassign ownership of packages.
claims.fix: Remove the blanket no-API claim and its open question. Replace the row's automation gap with the documented package-level call 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block', using the block reference already cited. Qualify the note: 'For an MCP server represented as a catalog package, the beta API blocks that package; this is not evidence that package blocking reproduces every server-component or gateway control.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview for MCP package applicability.
